title: deferred-preemption-and-kernel-aligned-coalescer-for-continuous-batcher
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Continuous batcher tails were suffering periodic p95 spikes for KV-heavy conversational workloads. Root cause analysis in ENG-4219 showed that aggressive preemption of KV-pinned slots and small misaligned coalescing windows caused repeated cold KV cache re-pins and kernel underutilization on A100 instances. This PR introduces two complementary runtime changes: 1) deferred preemption: when an incoming higher-priority request would preempt a KV-pinned slot, we schedule a short deferred-preempt window (configurable, default 15ms) to allow the current request to finish cheap KV writes or complete an aligned kernel launch to avoid re-pinning churn; 2) kernel-aligned coalescer: coalescing logic is adjusted to prefer grouping requests whose sequence-length distribution and model step counts align to common kernel sizes (64/128/256 token micro-batches), reducing partial-kernel launches and improving GPU utilization. Additionally, a lightweight affinity score is tracked per queue to bias admission toward slots that minimize cross-KV-set migrations. Changes: - runtime/scheduler/deferred_preempt.go: deferred preemption state machine, config knobs, metrics (deferred_preempt_count, deferred_preempt_latency_ms). - runtime/coalescer/kernel_align.go: new alignment heuristics and experiments flag. - runtime/kv/pin_manager.go: soft-kv-release path that attempts background unpin with jitter to avoid thundering re-pins. - config/defaults.yaml: new knobs: scheduler.deferred_preempt_ms, coalescer.alignment_threshold, kv.soft_release_jitter_ms. - tests/integration/continuous_batcher_affinity_test.go: synthetic KV-heavy scenarios and invariant checks. Benchmarks & results (internal lab, p99 is end-to-end for live traffic simulation): - Baseline (release/main) on 8xA100, conversational KV-heavy trace: p50: 18ms, p95: 132ms, p99: 287ms. - This branch: p50: 17.3ms (-4%), p95: 98ms (-26%), p99: 210ms (-27%). - GPU kernel occupancy increased on average +9% for the measured trace; per-request KV re-pin events down -42%. Cost impact: median tokens-per-second slightly improved; unit cost remained ~flat because fewer retries and tail spikes reduced overall overprovisioning requirements. Tests: unit, race, and integration suites pass. CI matrix: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, and a GPU-smoke job. Stability: configuration guarded behind a runtime feature flag 'scheduler_deferred_preempt' and rollout scheduled as canary then global. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated pools 2 -> 10 -> 100 (hosts), monitor deferred_preempt_count, p95 latency, and kv_pin_rate. Related: addresses regressions observed during SUP-1471 incident and dovetails with ongoing work on kv warmup heuristics (ENG-4330).
